coachingPoints: Sprint the first 70% of the distance, then chop your steps short for the last 30%
High hands on the catch — contest the shot before anything else
Use short, choppy steps on the approach so you can react to the drive
Read the defender's feet: a step toward you means drive, a plant means shot
Angle the closeout to send the drive toward help, not away from it
If beaten off the dribble, sprint to recover rather than reaching
commonMistakes: Flying past the shooter with long strides — chop steps to stay balanced
Closing out with hands down — the shot gets off uncontested
Closing out too close and fouling the jump shooter
Running straight at the man without an angle, giving up both shot and drive
description: Close the distance to a shooter under control: sprint, chop steps, high hands, and a contest without fouling.
gameSituations: Recovering to your man after a help rotation
Guarding a shooter who catches a skip pass
Defending a kick-out after your teammate helps on a drive
Any catch-and-shoot opportunity your man gets

howTo.detail: The moment the ball moves toward your man, sprint. The closeout starts before the catch, not after it. The first 70% of the distance is a dead sprint.
howTo.title: Sprint early to the shooter

howTo.detail: As you arrive, shorten your stride into quick choppy steps. This keeps your weight balanced so you can stop, react to a drive, or contest a shot.
howTo.title: Chop your steps on arrival

howTo.detail: Get your hands high as you arrive — one hand up to contest the shot. High hands force the shooter to hesitate and take away the quick trigger.
howTo.title: Hands high before the catch

howTo.detail: Aim your closeout at the shooter's inside shoulder to guide him toward your help. Never close out so straight that you give up a straight-line drive to the basket.
howTo.title: Take an angle that favors your help

howTo.detail: End the closeout in a low defensive stance, balanced and ready. From here you are on-ball defender: contain the drive, contest the shot.
howTo.title: Finish in stance, balanced

title: Closeouts
whatIsIt: A closeout is the sprint-and-stop movement a defender uses to get back to an offensive player who is about to receive the ball — usually a shooter. You are far from your man, the ball swings his way, and you must cover ground fast while still arriving under control.

The closeout is one of the most practiced and most misplayed actions in basketball. Done well, it takes away the shot and contains the drive. Done poorly — flying past the shooter out of control — it gives up the exact open drive or foul the defense was trying to prevent.
whyItMatters: Modern offenses are built to force closeouts: drive, kick, swing the ball, and make someone fly at a shooter. Every possession that ends in a rotation ends in a closeout somewhere. Teams that close out well can help aggressively and recover; teams that cannot are punished with open threes or blow-by drives all game.
